contracts.commit_point: FastAPI dependency resolution of Depends(_get_tenant) immediately before the /query handler body executes; rejection commits as HTTPException 401 inside _inner (auth.py:243-251).
contracts.declared_mechanism: get_current_tenant() dependency factory (auth.py:238-257) returns _inner, which raises HTTPException 401 for cred=None, undecodable/expired token, or unknown user before returning TenantInfo; instantiated once as _get_tenant (main.py:276) and attached to the route via tenant: TenantInfo = Depends(_get_tenant) (main.py:344).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A request to POST /query carrying no Bearer credential, a token that fails signature/expiry validation (decode_token returns None), or a token whose sub names no existing user being admitted to the handler instead of being rejected with HTTP 401.
pending_binding_information: Whether the admin-only 403 rule on POST /auth/register (main.py:294-302) merits a separate contract: user creation is not bound to any agent tool, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input in supplied source.
contracts.protected_operation: Handling of POST /query requests (the agent-invoking NL2SQL query endpoint).
contracts.protected_resource: POST /query route and the agent query pipeline it launches (apps/api/main.py).
contracts.protection_obligation: POST /query — the HTTP entry point that launches the SQL-reconciliation agent graph — must reject with HTTP 401 any request lacking a valid, non-expired JWT Bearer token bound to an existing user, before the handler (and any agent execution) runs.
scope_limits: Covers only routes declaring Depends(_get_tenant); supplied source shows many routes without it (/auth/login, /datasources*, /admin/reindex, /feedback, /kb/docs*, /agents*, /trace, /metrics, /health), which are outside this contract.
Token verification degrades when python-jose is absent: decode_token falls back to unsigned base64 with only an exp check (auth.py:114-122) and create_token is likewise unsigned (auth.py:103-105).

The same _get_tenant dependency also guards tenant-model-config routes, session CRUD, and /auth/register, but supplied source binds none of those operations to an agent tool, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input; they are excluded from this agent-mediated contract.
HTTPBearer(auto_error=False) (auth.py:43) makes a missing header surface as cred=None handled by the 401 branch rather than framework-level rejection.

contracts.commit_point: Return of the rejected state dict {'sql': 'REJECT', 'final_status': 'rejected', ...} (clarify.py:149-155; parallel branches at 157-165 and 168-180).
contracts.declared_mechanism: clarify_node calls is_safe(query) (clarify.py:132) and combines the verdict with DML/DDL keyword scanning and injection-pattern checks to return a rejected GraphState update.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A query for which verdict.is_safe is False and whose text contains 'drop '/'delete '/'update '/'insert '/'alter '/'truncate ' (or which contains '; --' or '/*') continuing through the pipeline rather than being rejected at the clarify node.
pending_binding_information: recon_v2/orchestration/graph.py (build_graph) is not supplied; clarify_node's placement inside the executed graph is supported by the state dataflow (main.py:394-417 initial_state/graph.invoke → GraphState/ctx_registry → clarify.py:122-125), not by graph wiring source.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent graph processing of the user query at clarify_node (GraphState screening).
contracts.protected_resource: Downstream target database / SQL execution path of the reconciliation agent.
contracts.protection_obligation: User queries entering the agent orchestration graph that are judged unsafe by is_safe and match DML/DDL keywords, or that carry injection patterns ('; --' or '/*'), must be short-circuited by the clarify node into a rejected GraphState ('sql': 'REJECT', final_status 'rejected') instead of proceeding toward SQL generation/execution.
scope_limits: Rejection requires both an unsafe verdict and a matching keyword (or an injection pattern); an unsafe verdict without those text patterns falls through to the clarification flow rather than rejection.
The committed effect of this contract is the rejected graph state; database-side commit points are covered by separate sql_runner and SQLTool contracts.
boundary_edge write-op rejection (clarify.py:168-180) uses a broader keyword list including 'create' but applies only when intent == 'boundary_edge'.

contracts.commit_point: self.adapter.execute(sql) at sql_runner.py:84, reached only after the safety, dialect-adaptation, LIMIT, and EXPLAIN steps pass.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Step-1 guard is_safe(inp.sql, dialect) in _run returning success=False 'safety rejected' before further steps; apply_limit_guard appends LIMIT 1000 when inp.apply_limit (default True) and no LIMIT present; adapter.explain() pre-validation must succeed before execute; ToolBase.run enforces Pydantic input validation before _run.
contracts.forbidden_condition: inp.sql whose is_safe verdict is unsafe (empty, unparseable, not rooted in SELECT/WITH, or containing Delete/Update/Insert/Drop/Alter/Create/TruncateTable/Command nodes) being passed to self.adapter.execute(); secondarily, a SELECT lacking LIMIT being executed when the LIMIT guard is enabled.
pending_binding_information: No supplied view shows the orchestration node dispatching sql_runner with model-generated SQL (sql_gen/execute node and ToolRegistry dispatch implementation not provided); mediation is established via registration into the default ToolRegistry wired to ctx.tools plus OpenAI function-schema exposure (base.py:81-91), not an observed dispatch call site.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of agent-supplied SQL via the sql_runner tool (SQLRunnerTool._run).
contracts.protected_resource: Target SQL databases reachable through SQLAdapter (SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL).
contracts.protection_obligation: During agent tool use, SQLRunnerTool must reject — before any database execution — any SQL failing the sql_safety read-only check (root verb SELECT/WITH only; no DML/DDL/Command nodes; parse failure rejects), and must by default auto-append LIMIT 1000 to SELECTs lacking one, so only bounded read-only SQL reaches SQLAdapter.execute().
scope_limits: LIMIT 1000 is applied only when inp.apply_limit is True (default per SQLRunnerInput); a caller may set apply_limit=False and execute SELECTs without LIMIT.
Guard covers only the sql_runner tool path; recon_core SQLTool and any direct adapter usage are separate surfaces with their own guards.
is_safe rejects parse failures ('prefer false positives' design), so dialect-valid syntax sqlglot cannot parse is also rejected.
adapter.explain()/execute() implementations are not in supplied views; pre-validation behavior is taken from the call site contract only.

contracts.declared_mechanism: Inline keyword blacklist on sql.strip().upper() (startswith or ' KEYWORD ' containment) returning an error string before sqlite3.connect/c.execute; the sql_validate sub-tool applies the same blacklist before EXPLAIN parsing.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A statement beginning with, or containing space-delimited, any blacklisted keyword reaching c.execute(sql).
pending_binding_information: No supplied view registers SQLTool into a running agent: recon_v2's build_default_registry registers SQLRunnerTool (tools/__init__.py:29) and recon_core registry/agent wiring is not provided; agent_entry_binding role omitted and mediation recorded as not_established.
contracts.protection_obligation: The recon_core SQLTool sql_execute sub-tool must reject any SQL whose normalized text starts with or contains a blacklisted DML/DDL keyword (DROP/DELETE/UPDATE/INSERT/ALTER/CREATE) before executing it against the tool's SQLite database.
scope_limits: Blacklist is startswith/space-delimited containment on uppercased text; statements not matching those exact patterns (keyword embedded without surrounding spaces, PRAGMA/ATTACH, appended statements) fall outside the declared condition.
The parent SQLTool.run refuses direct invocation (sql_tool.py:32-37); only expanded sub-tools are executable.
sql_validate shares the blacklist but only EXPLAIN-parses; it imposes no runtime guard on sql_execute.

missing_information: recon_v2/orchestration/graph.py (build_graph) is not supplied; clarify_node's registration inside the executed graph is inferred from the state dataflow only.

No supplied view shows the orchestration node that dispatches SQLRunnerTool with model-generated SQL; the sql_gen node and recon_v2/tools/registry.py dispatch implementation are outside the provided views.
SQLAdapter.execute/explain semantics (mutation capability, commit behavior) are not in supplied views; the database effect stratum is assigned from the execute call site.
